'''Ju-Lee Kim''' ({{lang|ko|김주리}}, born 1969) is a South Korean mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). Her research involves the [[representation theory]] of [[Pro-p group|''p''-adic groups]].<ref name="profile">{{citation|url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=132|title=Ju-Lee Kim|work=MIT Mathematics People|publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|accessdate=2015-11-20|archive-date=2021-01-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114120248/https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=132|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Kim completed her undergraduate studies at [[KAIST]] in 1991,<ref name="profile"/> and earned a Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1997 supervised by [[Roger Evans Howe|Roger Howe]];<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=14937}}</ref> at Yale, she was also mentored by [[Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro]].

After postdoctoral study at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and the [[École Normale Supérieure]], she joined the faculty as an assistant professor at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1998.<ref name="bio">{{citation|url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=132|title=Ju-Lee Kim|work=MIT Directory|publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|accessdate=2020-05-31|archive-date=2021-01-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114120248/https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=132|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kim joined the faculty at [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 2002, and then moved to MIT in 2007.<ref name="mwim">{{citation|url=https://math.mit.edu/wim/members/ju-lee-kim/|title=Ju-Lee Kim|work=MIT Women in Mathematics|publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|accessdate=2020-05-31}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to the representation theory of semisimple groups over nonarchimedean local fields and for service to the profession."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-20}}</ref>

==Personal==
Her husband, [[Paul Seidel]], is also a mathematician at MIT.<ref name="mwim"/>
